edits.new: The Bicep resource is Microsoft.Network/privateEndpoints. Its properties include subnet (with id) and manualPrivateLinkServiceConnections, whose connection properties include privateLinkServiceId (the resource ID of the private link service). For Atlas on Azure, the target is the Atlas-provisioned private link service, whose resource ID is /subscriptions/{SUBSCRIPTION-ID}/resourceGroups/{RESOURCE-GROUP-ID}/providers/Microsoft.Network/privateLinkServices/{ENDPOINT-SERVICE-NAME}, built from the endpoint service name that Atlas returns (for example pls_<atlas private endpoint ID>), not the Atlas project ID. Sources: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/microsoft.network/privateendpoints ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-cluster-private-endpoint.md

edits.rationale: The Microsoft schema supports the resource type, subnet, manualPrivateLinkServiceConnections and privateLinkServiceId. The Atlas tutorial builds the private link service resource ID from the Atlas-returned endpoint service name and passes it to the Azure private endpoint with manual request enabled. No pinned page says in so many words not to use the project ID, so that part is rephrased as what Atlas actually uses. Atlas's own placeholders are a resource-group ID beginning rg_ and an endpoint service name, so 'Atlas-provided service resource ID' is a composed ID, not a single value Atlas hands over.
